items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: They only cut that one record under that name. That's all. Walter Page and these Blue Devils.

ctx.x: No, I never cut with them. That was Count Basie was in there and I remember the band real well because I was with Troy's band and we had competition there. So, I would stay in my backyard as they say unless I was really needed.

They only cut that one record under that name. That's all. Walter Page and these Blue Devils. Blue Devils. That's correct. Yeah. I had that record at one time, Bill, and it ended up in Baker's collection.
Yeah. I had picked up one and it was Cracked one time. Everybody got a good one.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Yes, we had battles with them, and also jammed together after hours.

ctx.x: And did you have battles with them?
Yes, we had battles with them, and also jammed together after hours. Orrin Lips Page was one of the really great trumpet players, too. I think he died a few years ago in England.
Yes, he's dead now. That's right. Were these, you'd say Troy Floyd's band was a happy band, or they were all happy together?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: So they thought that Lips Page and Oren and the Brothers weren't even related.

ctx.x: Well now you're talking about blues and Judy Williams and all that. Did you know Lips Fades when you were in fact?

Lips and I played together. Lips came to Dallas, Texas in 1926 with Benny Moulton's Blue Devils. And Basie was the pianist in this band. And Oren Page was the bass. So they thought that Lips Page and Oren and the Brothers weren't even related. And Page and I, we used to go out at night and sit out and play with each other. And Compton with John on the piano.
Well what about his style then? Beautiful. Great style. Did he sound the same as he did on the record with, say, LATER in 32?
